ai.description: *Microhyla chakrapanii* is a small frog (17–20 mm) with a brownish-grey dorsum and a dark lateral band. It is distinguished by a pointed snout and a lack of webbing on the toes. Family: Microhylidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Microhyla chakrapanii* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark, W-shaped or chevron-like marking on its back, which is absent in most other Indian congeners.
ai.habitat: *Microhyla chakrapanii* inhabits the leaf litter of tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the Andaman Islands, typically found at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: Microhyla chakrapanii is primarily nocturnal, emerging during the monsoon season to forage for small invertebrates in leaf litter and moist soil habitats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Microhyla chakrapanii* breeds during the monsoon season, laying eggs in small, temporary water bodies. Details on specific clutch size remain scientifically undocumented.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Microhyla chakrapanii* is endemic to the Andaman Islands in the Bay of Bengal, occurring at low elevations within this Indian archipelago.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Microhyla chakrapanii* consists of a high-pitched, insect-like trill, typically emitted by males calling from shallow, stagnant forest pools.
